data.narrative:
SpaceForest is a publicly traded (GPW) company in Space & Aerospace founded by Robert Magiera, Andrzej Magiera, and Jerzy Michalski. The sector comprises 13 observable peers: 5 public companies (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private entities including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, ICEYE, Sierra Space, and Planet Labs.

Two standard valuation methods were evaluated. Peer-median triangulation proved inapplicable: while 14 same-sector peers exist, none met narrow filtering criteria (same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier benchmarks requiring ≥3 datapoints). A sector-wide median would obscure material differences in company maturity and business model. Public-comparable anchoring using the Space & Aerospace P/S median of 24.6x across the 6 public tickers also could not be executed, as SpaceForest's revenue figure is not on file—a common data gap for newly public companies in this sector.

The absence of applicable quantitative methods indicates that meaningful valuation synthesis cannot proceed from the available dataset. Establishing a defensible range would require either: disclosure of SpaceForest's current-period revenue to enable P/S application; identification of ≥3 sufficiently comparable peers at an adjacent stage; or additional financial metrics (EBITDA, FCF, customer concentration). Until such data surfaces, valuation should be deferred. The primary uncertainty is not methodological but informational.
